evidence: This is supported by HOMER motif analysis of ATAC-seq data.

claim: The expression level of DARPP-32 was decreased in E18.5 Foxf2-null mice.

source: Moreover, although the expression level of DARPP-32 was decreased (Figure 5D), the presence of diffuse DARPP-32-immunopositive cells in the striatum of E18.5 Foxf2-null mice (Figure 5C) suggests that the early born MSNs migrate to the striatal mantle, but other elements required for striosome organization are impacted.

evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in the figure.

source: The extended overexpression of Foxp2, however, implies an element of a long-lasting effect on striosomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the RT-qPCR data showing maintained Foxp2 expression.

claim: Adenoviral-mediated overexpression of human FOXF2 promoted an increase in the percentage of DARPP-32-immunopositive cells in primary mouse neuronal cultures derived from embryonic striatum.
source: Similar to early postnatal striatum in vivo, adenoviral-mediated overexpression of human FOXF2 promoted an increase in the percentage of DARPP-32-immunopositive cells in primary mouse neuronal cultures derived from embryonic striatum (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in the figure.

claim: There was an increase in striosome (Oprm1, Foxp2, Rasgrp1) and matrix (Calb1, Rasgrp2, and EphA4) marker mRNAs in wild-type primary striatal neurons transduced with ADV-FOXF2-mCherry.
source: There was also an increase in striosome (Oprm1, Foxp2, Rasgrp1) and matrix (Calb1, Rasgrp2, and EphA4) marker mRNAs in wild-type primary striatal neurons transduced with ADV-FOXF2-mCherry (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), again suggesting that Foxf2 likely has an effect on overall striatal development, not restricted to striosomes.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in the figure.

claim: Foxf2 likely has an effect on overall striatal development, not restricted to striosomes.
source: There was also an increase in striosome (Oprm1, Foxp2, Rasgrp1) and matrix (Calb1, Rasgrp2, and EphA4) marker mRNAs in wild-type primary striatal neurons transduced with ADV-FOXF2-mCherry (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A), again suggesting that Foxf2 likely has an effect on overall striatal development, not restricted to striosomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the RT-qPCR data showing effects on both striosome and matrix markers.

claim: On PND3, Olig2 protein co-localizes with DARPP-32 in striosomes.
source: On PND3, Olig2 protein co-localizes with DARPP-32 in striosomes, and individual Olig2-immunopositive cells devoid of DARPP-32 signal are visible throughout the striatum, likely representing oligodendroglial lineage cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in the figure.

claim: Individual Olig2-immunopositive cells devoid of DARPP-32 signal are visible throughout the striatum on PND3, likely representing oligodendroglial lineage cells.
source: On PND3, Olig2 protein co-localizes with DARPP-32 in striosomes, and individual Olig2-immunopositive cells devoid of DARPP-32 signal are visible throughout the striatum, likely representing oligodendroglial lineage cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is an inference based on the known expression of Olig2 in oligodendrocyte lineage cells.

claim: Olig2 mRNA largely colocalized with DARPP-32 mRNA in striosomes on PND3.
source: Olig2 mRNA also largely colocalized with DARPP-32 mRNA in striosomes (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by RNAscope data shown in the figure.

claim: Olig2 protein is cytoplasmic in distribution in the striosomes, but is nuclear in the non-neuronal cells.
source: Note in the IHC that Olig2 protein is cytoplasmic in distribution in the striosomes, but is nuclear in the non-neuronal cells.
evidence: This is an observation from the immunohistochemistry data.

claim: An OCR 4.4 kb downstream of the Olig2 gene is restricted to EGFP+ samples.
source: We compared the Olig2 ATAC-seq tracks from EGFP+ and EGFP– cells and identified a peak 4.4 kb downstream of the Olig2 gene (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in the figure.

claim: The putative Olig2 enhancer (chr16:91,233,041–91,234,111) drives mCherry reporter expression in striosomes on PND3.
source: We cloned the putative Olig2 enhancer (chr16:91,233,041–91,234,111) into an mCherry reporter plasmid containing only the core hsp68 promoter (Hauberg et al., 2020; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) and obtained 14 positive founders after pronuclear injection. mCherry was expressed in 9/9 founders on PND3 and co-localized with DARPP-32 neurons in the striosome (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by transgenic reporter data shown in the figure.

claim: mCherry driven by the Olig2 enhancer was expressed in 9/9 founders on PND3 and co-localized with DARPP-32 neurons in the striosome.
source: We cloned the putative Olig2 enhancer (chr16:91,233,041–91,234,111) into an mCherry reporter plasmid containing only the core hsp68 promoter (Hauberg et al., 2020; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) and obtained 14 positive founders after pronuclear injection. mCherry was expressed in 9/9 founders on PND3 and co-localized with DARPP-32 neurons in the striosome (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by transgenic reporter data shown in the figure.

claim: mCherry driven by the Olig2 enhancer was also expressed in individual cells in the matrix which are DARPP-32-negative, probably representing cells of the oligodendroglial lineage.
source: mCherry was also expressed in individual cells in the matrix which are DARPP-32-negative (indicated by arrowheads), and probably again represent cells of the oligodendroglial lineage.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known expression of Olig2 in oligodendrocyte lineage cells.

claim: The Olig2 enhancer-driven transgenic reporter was expressed in 2/5 founders assayed as adults, but its expression was low and absent in NeuN+ neurons.
source: The transgenic reporter was expressed in 2/5 founders assayed as adults, but its expression was low and absent in NeuN+ neurons (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in the figure.

claim: Homozygote Olig2 knockout animals survived until late on the day of birth.
source: Homozygote animals survived until late on the day of birth, so brains were assayed early on the day of birth.
evidence: This is an observation about the Olig2 knockout mouse phenotype.

claim: Striosomes were absent in Olig2 P0-null mice, particularly in the anterior striatum.
source: Remarkably, striosomes were absent, particularly in the anterior striatum (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in the figure.

claim: DARPP-32 immunopositive neurons were essentially undetectable in the Olig2 P0-null striatum.
source: DARPP-32 immunopositive neurons were essentially undetectable in the Olig2 P0-null striatum, and although we have not yet identified the exact mechanism, the data suggest either regulation of Ppp1r1b gene expression by Olig2 and/or failure of striosome neurogenesis or migration.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data.

claim: The data suggest either regulation of Ppp1r1b gene expression by Olig2 and/or failure of striosome neurogenesis or migration in Olig2 knockout mice.
source: DARPP-32 immunopositive neurons were essentially undetectable in the Olig2 P0-null striatum, and although we have not yet identified the exact mechanism, the data suggest either regulation of Ppp1r1b gene expression by Olig2 and/or failure of striosome neurogenesis or migration.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism based on the observed phenotype.

claim: Quantitation of striosome and matrix markers in Olig2 P0-null mice revealed a marked decrease in Ppp1r1b, Oprm1, and Foxp2.
source: Quantitation of striosome and matrix markers in these mice revealed a marked decrease in Ppp1r1b, Oprm1, and Foxp2 (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in the figure.

claim: Intracerebroventricular injection of AAV-CMV-Olig2-IRES-EGFP on P0 resulted in a decrease in Oprm1 and Foxp2 mRNAs, but an increase in Rasgrp1.
source: We also performed intracerebroventricular injection of AAV-CMV-Olig2-IRES-EGFP on P0, and analyzed the effect of Olig2 overexpression on MSN markers, and surprisingly, found a decrease in Oprm1 and Foxp2 mRNAs, but an increase in Rasgrp1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E,F), indicating a mixed effect on the striosomes, which requires further exploration.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in the figure.

claim: Olig2 overexpression has a mixed effect on the striosomes, which requires further exploration.
source: We also performed intracerebroventricular injection of AAV-CMV-Olig2-IRES-EGFP on P0, and analyzed the effect of Olig2 overexpression on MSN markers, and surprisingly, found a decrease in Oprm1 and Foxp2 mRNAs, but an increase in Rasgrp1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E,F), indicating a mixed effect on the striosomes, which requires further exploration.
evidence: This is an inference based on the RT-qPCR data showing mixed effects.

claim: Adenovirus-mediated expression of OLIG2 does not increase the number of DARPP-32-immunopositive cells in primary mouse MSNs.
source: Adenovirus-mediated expression of OLIG2 does not increase the number of DARPP-32-immunopositive cells, but importantly, it increases levels of the mRNAs for striosome markers Oprm1, Foxp2 and Rasgrp1.
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data.

claim: Adenovirus-mediated expression of OLIG2 increases levels of the mRNAs for striosome markers Oprm1, Foxp2 and Rasgrp1 in primary mouse MSNs.
source: Adenovirus-mediated expression of OLIG2 does not increase the number of DARPP-32-immunopositive cells, but importantly, it increases levels of the mRNAs for striosome markers Oprm1, Foxp2 and Rasgrp1.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data.

claim: The average rank of Stat3 is 4.5 in the striosome network, which ranks at the top.
source: The ranking was based on the number of edges expanding from each node and the number of overlapping TFs shared between nodes that interact with Nr4a1. Among the 58 TFs in the striosome network, the average rank of Stat3 is 4.5, which ranks at the top.
evidence: This is supported by network analysis.

claim: Stat1 is the TF that regulated the greatest number of differentially expressed TFs (314 out of 811) in the gene regulatory network.
source: We also built the gene regulatory network, including all differentially expressed TFs, set through the regulatory data curated by ORegAnno database (Lesurf et al., 2016), which identified Stat1 as the TF that regulated the greatest number of differentially expressed TFs (314 out of 811) (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by gene regulatory network analysis.

claim: Both Stat1 and Stat3 are enriched in the EGFP+ cells.
source: Both Stat1 and Stat3 are enriched in the EGFP+ cells (Figure 2—source data 1), so together with the in-silico analyses, these data suggest that the STAT pathway is a key regulating pathway during the differentiation of striosome neurons.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data.

claim: The STAT pathway is a key regulating pathway during the differentiation of striosome neurons.
source: Both Stat1 and Stat3 are enriched in the EGFP+ cells (Figure 2—source data 1), so together with the in-silico analyses, these data suggest that the STAT pathway is a key regulating pathway during the differentiation of striosome neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on RNA-seq data and network analysis.

claim: STAT1 overexpression increased the number of DARPP-32-immunopositive cells in primary mouse MSNs.
source: STAT1 overexpression increased the number of DARPP-32-immunopositive cells (Figure 7B,C) and increased the mRNA levels of striosome markers Ppp1r1b, Oprm1, Foxp2, Foxf2, and Olig2, as well as the matrix marker Calb1 (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in the figure.

claim: STAT1 overexpression increased the mRNA levels of striosome markers Ppp1r1b, Oprm1, Foxp2, Foxf2, and Olig2, as well as the matrix marker Calb1 in primary mouse MSNs.
source: STAT1 overexpression increased the number of DARPP-32-immunopositive cells (Figure 7B,C) and increased the mRNA levels of striosome markers Ppp1r1b, Oprm1, Foxp2, Foxf2, and Olig2, as well as the matrix marker Calb1 (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in the figure.

claim: The upregulation of Foxf2 and Olig2 by STAT1 suggests that these two TFs may be downstream of Stat1.
source: Particularly notable is the upregulation of Foxf2 and Olig2, suggesting that these two TFs may be downstream of Stat1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the RT-qPCR data.

claim: STAT1 overexpression, with or without FOXF2, increases the number of OPRM1-immunopositive cells in HD-iPSC-derived NSCs.
source: STAT1 overexpression, with or without FOXF2, increases the number of OPRM1-immunopositive cells (Figure 8A), with OLIG2 producing a trend in the same direction.
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in the figure.

claim: OLIG2 overexpression produces a trend toward increasing the number of OPRM1-immunopositive cells in HD-iPSC-derived NSCs.
source: STAT1 overexpression, with or without FOXF2, increases the number of OPRM1-immunopositive cells (Figure 8A), with OLIG2 producing a trend in the same direction.
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in the figure.

claim: STAT1 and OLIG2 together increase the expression of PPP1R1B in HD-iPSC-derived NSCs.
source: STAT1 and OLIG2 together also increase the expression of PPP1R1B (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in the figure.

claim: STAT1 and FOXF2 in combination induce RASGRP1 in HD-iPSC-derived NSCs, although to a lesser extent than OLIG2 alone.
source: Alone, only OLIG2 increases RASGRP1 and EPHA4 mRNAs, but in combination, STAT1 and FOXF2 induce RASGRP1, although to a lesser extent.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data.

claim: RASGRP2, a marker of the matrix, largely behaves inversely to RASGRP1 in HD-iPSC-derived NSCs.
source: Interestingly, RASGRP2, a marker of the matrix, largely behaves inversely to RASGRP1, consistent with their expression in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data and is consistent with in vivo expression patterns.

claim: OLIG2 alone increases the matrix marker CALB1 mRNA in HD-iPSC-derived NSCs, but at a lower-fold than the striosome markers.
source: OLIG2 alone also increases the matrix marker CALB1 mRNA, but at a lower-fold than the striosome markers.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data.

claim: In contrast to its effect in primary MSNs, FOXF2 alone increased only RASGRP2 in HD-iPSC-derived NSCs, and did not even increase TUJ1.
source: Notably, in contrast to its effect in primary MSNs, FOXF2 alone increased only RASGRP2, and did not even increase TUJ1, a marker of pan-neuronal differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data.

claim: FOXF2 alone failed to induce expression of BCL11B mRNA in HD-iPSC-derived NSCs.
source: Along with the in vivo absence of striosome compartmentation in the striatum despite the presence of Ppp1r1b neurons, these data may indicate an early role restricted to compartmentation and not overall phenotypic maturation as defined by expression of gene markers. In agreement with this hypothesis, FOXF2 alone failed to induce expression of BCL11B mRNA, a transcription factor required for striatal development (Arlotta et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data and citation.

claim: The data may indicate an early role for FOXF2 restricted to compartmentation and not overall phenotypic maturation as defined by expression of gene markers.
source: Along with the in vivo absence of striosome compartmentation in the striatum despite the presence of Ppp1r1b neurons, these data may indicate an early role restricted to compartmentation and not overall phenotypic maturation as defined by expression of gene markers.
evidence: This is an inference based on the in vivo and in vitro data.

claim: Expression of FOXF2, OLIG2 and STAT in HD NSCs resulted in an increase expression of pan neuronal marker Nestin.
source: As expected, expression of FOXF2, OLIG2 and STAT in HD NSCs resulted in an increase expression of pan neuronal marker Nestin (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in the figure.

claim: OLIG2/STAT1 clearly induce OPRM1 expression in isogenic control C116-NSCs.
source: Similar results were observed in isogenic controls C116-NSCs (Figure 8—figure supplement 2), in which OLIG2/STAT1 clearly induce OPRM1 expression.
evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in the figure.

claim: FOXF2, OLIG2, and STAT expression provides a rapid differentiation of DARPP-32 MSNs with high levels of MOR expression within 4 days.
source: FOXF2, OLIG2, and STAT expression provides a rapid differentiation of DARPP-32 MSNs with high levels of MOR expression within 4 days.
evidence: This is supported by the immunocytochemistry and RT-qPCR data.

claim: Current MSN protocols require 20–50 days of culture and do not generate striosomal MSN subtypes.
source: Current MSN protocols require 20–50 days of culture and do not generate striosomal MSN subtypes (Arber et al., 2015; Golas, 2018; Kemp et al., 2016; Telezhkin et al., 2016; Victor et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.
